title: Welsh Rarebit
subtitle: Toasted bread with a grilled cheese and ale sauce
excerpt: Thick toast spread with a sauce of melted cheddar, Welsh ale, mustard, and Worcestershire sauce, then grilled until bubbling and spotted brown. More than cheese on toast.

recipe.sourceNotes: Welsh rarebit (originally 'Welsh rabbit', a joke name suggesting the Welsh ate cheese as a substitute for the rabbit they could not afford) has been recorded since at least 1725. The dish is a cooked cheese sauce applied to toast, distinct from plain cheese on toast. The sauce is made by melting cheese into a roux or directly into ale, with mustard, Worcestershire sauce, and egg yolk to add depth and richness. Hannah Glasse's 'The Art of Cookery Made Plain and Easy' (1747) is among the early sources. It is still the most popular savoury cheese-on-toast dish in Britain.

content.text: The cheese sauce is distinct from plain melted cheese: it is thickened and enriched, and should be thick enough to spread onto the toast without running off the sides. Toast the bread on both sides before spreading the sauce: the toast must be able to support the sauce under the grill without going soggy. Watch the grill closely once the sauce is on. It browns in seconds.
Melt the butter in a small saucepan over low heat. Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute. Pour in the ale and stir until smooth and thickened, about 2 minutes.

Remove from the heat. Stir in the cheese, mustard, Worcestershire sauce, egg yolk, and black pepper until the cheese has melted and the sauce is smooth. The sauce should be thick enough to hold its shape when spread.
Toast the bread on both sides under the grill. Spread the cheese sauce generously onto each slice. Return to the grill for 2 to 3 minutes until bubbling and spotted brown. Serve at once.
